W.note: Syllables 5-7-5 (Late in autumn wind / a lens above the ridge stands / while the air runs through); a lenticular cloud drawn as a stationary lens while air streams past is an accurate, unnamed evocation, with a clean turn from wind to stillness.

X.note: Syllables 5-7-5 (Pearl-lit, high, unseen / na-cre-ous clouds bloom at dusk / winter's rarest sky); it names nacreous clouds accurately for altitude and dusk timing, but 'winter's rarest sky' is a stock closing phrase and the poem does not turn.

Y.note: Syllables 5-7-5 (Na-cre-ous glow spreads / across the winter dusk sky / clouds no one expects); the nacreous naming and dusk glow are accurate, but 'clouds no one expects' is a generic turn and the glow is less seen than the other entries.

Z.note: Syllables 4-7-4 (midwinter dusk / a thin veil above the ridge / turns pearl, then gray), a deliberate short-long-short shape that falls one syllable short per outer line; the veil fading from pearl to gray is a true nacreous behavior and gives the strongest feeling of change.
